- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak or use moving average to smooth.
- In low sentiment (≤0.3) environments, model often underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day moving average of true values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment > 0.6, reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment spikes.
